subject: Reserved GPU plan: traffic profile & burst checklist
messages:
From: Caroline Park <caroline@atlasai.com>
To: nikhil_sharma@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Fleet sizing & burst profile for Reserved GPU plan

Hi Nikhil,

We're kicking off planning for a reserved GPU commitment and need a quick read on whether Redwood Dedicated makes sense for Atlas. High level details below — can you confirm what ballpark fleet size we'd need, and what follow-up artifacts you need from us?

Quick context: Atlas AI runs a multimodal LLM assistant for enterprise customers (search + summarization + short-form generation). We're targeting a January reserved-start if numbers look reasonable.

Workload snapshot (typical/expected):
- Model: LlamaX-70B quantized (we're flexible to variants)
- Typical prompt length (user input): 120 tokens
- Typical generated output (completion): mean 340 tokens, p95 600 tokens
- Average steady QPS: 40 requests/sec across the region (us-west2)
- Peak concurrency (sessions actively generating): 220 concurrent sessions
- Short bursts: daily marketing-driven spikes ~900 concurrent for ~90-150 seconds (once per day)
- Latency target: p99 <= 250ms (end-to-end for generation)
- Mostly streaming-enabled clients; some batch/async for long outputs

Questions we hope you can help with:
1) Rough GPU count (and suggested GPU family) to meet p99 250ms under steady and burst with reasonable autoscale/burst policies
2) Do you recommend a dedicated reserved pool vs. mix of reserved + hosted fallback?
3) What telemetry/artifacts would help your sizing (sample traffic CSV, histograms for token length, top prompt templates, etc.)

I've looped in procurement (procurement@atlasai.com) for timelines. Happy to provide a sample telemetry export if helpful — I can attach next message.

Thanks,
Caroline
Caroline Park
Head of Infrastructure
Atlas AI

From: nikhil_sharma@redwood.com
To: Caroline Park <caroline@atlasai.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, tessa_morgan@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fleet sizing & burst profile for Reserved GPU plan

Hi Caroline — thanks for the clear snapshot, this is very helpful. Quick clarifying questions so we don't over/under-provision:

1) Request mix: what fraction of traffic is chat-style (many short prompts + streaming) vs. long-batch generation? If you can give % or example day split, that helps a lot.
2) Session duration: for the 220 concurrent sessions, what's the average active generation time per session (seconds) and are those sequential multi-step conversations that reuse a long prefix?
3) Caching/prefix reuse: do you expect significant prefix/KV reuse across requests (e.g., system prompts, shared context), or are prompts mostly unique?
4) Sampling params: temperature/top_k/top_p typical values? Top-k sampling can impact latency budget.
5) Do you need encryption-at-rest with customer-managed keys (KMS) for the model snapshots? Any SOC2/Audit constraints that affect placement?
6) Do you require strict cold-start limits (i.e., no >1s cold starts) or is some tail acceptable during burst?

Attachments: I'm including a lightweight checklist we typically ask for in sizing conversations (pre-sales-snapshot.xlsx) — if you can fill the short CSV example with a day of telemetry that matches your peak day, that will let us run an internal sizing sim.

Initial thinking (very rough): given the burst shape you described (900 conc for ~2m/day) we'd likely recommend a reserved pool sized for 250–300 steady concurrency with autoscale burst capacity (shadow pool / pre-warmed instances) to hit the 900 short spikes with minimal cold starts. Exact GPU counts depend heavily on model variant, batching strategy, and KV reuse.

I'll propose a short technical workshop (30–45m) with our dedicated runtime team to validate assumptions and run a quick sim on sample telemetry. Would Thursday or Friday next week work for you?

Best,
Nikhil Sharma
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
nkh@redwood.com

From: Caroline Park <caroline@atlasai.com>

Cc: Atlas AI Procurement <procurement@atlasai.com>
Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 08:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fleet sizing & burst profile for Reserved GPU plan

Thanks Nikhil — answers inline below and attached a small sample telemetry export (sample_telemetry.csv).

1) Request mix: ~78% chat-style (short prompts + streaming), ~22% long-batch (async jobs).
2) Session duration: average active generation time per chat session is ~3.8s; however ~12% of sessions have multi-step flows where we append ~200 extra tokens across follow-ups (these tend to reuse the same prefix).
3) Caching/prefix reuse: high reuse of system prompt + user profile chunks across ~60% of requests (good KV cache hit rate expected).
4) Sampling params: temp 0.7, top_p 0.9, top_k 40.
4b) We do sometimes run deterministic jobs (temp 0.0) for customer reports — those are the long-batch jobs.
5) Compliance: SOC2 is required; KMS for customer-sensitive model artifacts would be nice but not a blocker for the first reserved contract.
6) Cold-starts: we'd like cold-starts to be below ~500ms for the majority of requests; occasional 1s+ on tail is acceptable during extreme burst.

Growth: plan to grow Q1 2027 by +35% traffic (primarily daytime peak).

Attachments: sample_telemetry.csv (includes per-request tokens, timestamp, latency, client-id). Let me know if you need a different format.

Would Friday 10:00am PT for the tech workshop work?

Cheers,
Caroline

Subject: Re: Fleet sizing & burst profile for Reserved GPU plan — preliminary recommendation & next steps

Caroline — thank you for the telemetry and the clear answers. We ran a quick internal sim with the sample CSV and the assumptions you provided. Below is a conservative, production-oriented preliminary recommendation and an ask list for the workshop.

Summary (preliminary):
- Model baseline: LlamaX-70B (quantized, fp16 or 4-bit for dedicated)
- Steady target concurrency (buffered): 300 concurrent-generation slots (accounts for 35% growth headroom)
- Short daily burst: plan for 900 concurrent with a 20% pre-warmed shadow pool to reduce cold-start risk
- Suggested GPU footprint: 8 x H100-80GB class nodes (reserved) with autoscale policy to bring up an additional 4–6 nodes from reserved/burst pool within 60s. If you prefer smaller SKUs, equivalent would be ~14 x A100-40GB-class nodes (depends on quantization).
- Batching: aggressive batching (target batch size 24–32) + KV cache reuse should keep p99 under 250ms for most steady traffic; streaming tails may still see p99 noise during extreme peaks — shadow pre-warming mitigates that.
- Fallback plan: recommend reserved + hosted fallback policy (hosted smaller model at slightly lower quality) for catastrophic overloads or regional outages.

Cost & procurement note: attached a ballpark_pricing.pdf with a rough monthly estimate for the recommended reserved footprint plus a buffer for burst credits. This is a preliminary estimate only; we'll refine after the workshop and a final traffic pass.

Next steps (workshop & artifacts):
1) Workshop (30–45m) — confirm Friday 10:00am PT works; we'll invite runtime and product engineers and run a short sim on your telemetry.
2) Fill the small CSV with a sample high-peak day (if possible include 3 days) — your sample_telemetry.csv looks great for the quick sim, 3 days helps shape autoscale ramp parameters.
3) Procurement info: if you can share a preferred start window for a reserved contract and any internal approval timelines, Marissa will coordinate the commercial proposal.
4) Optional: if you have any must-have compliance items (KMS/HSM, VPC requirements), send them before the workshop.

Links & artifacts:
- Capacity workbook (preview): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c_capacity_workbook
- HubSpot trial record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/contact/98765

I'll attach the pre-sales-snapshot.xlsx we referenced and the ballpark_pricing.pdf. Marissa will lead the commercial follow-up.

If that plan looks good we'll lock the workshop and draft an initial mutual action plan.

Best regards,
Nikhil Sharma
